Hi all,
My name is Kevin Zhang and I'm currently a research scientist at a startup, after having recently finished a PhD in Computer Science. A long time ago I was a pure mathematics undergrad but haven't touched math much since then (outside of the small amount I needed for CS research). As of late I've been thinking about math more, especially because of the news about AI usage for math.

As for my mathematical interests, I'm particularly fond of geometric dissection problems. I've done some computational work on this which I've put on my personal website:

  • https://sideprojects--wondrous-brigadeiros-fd4d90.netlify.app/projects/dissect/demo/index.html (coded pre-ChatGPT!)
  • https://sideprojects--wondrous-brigadeiros-fd4d90.netlify.app/projects/3d-scissors-congruence/demo/index.html (post ChatGPT...)

Recently, I've become interested in formalizing these dissections. In general, computational geometry algorithms suffer from many precision related issues so it would be nice to have efficient ways of verifying their correctness. I'm currently working on a little library that uses exact arithmetic in algebraic number fields to certify the correctness of my dissections, because often they involve only algebraic numbers and not reals in general.

I would, however, like to work on more general systems for certifying the correctness of computational geometry algorithms which operate on real numbers in general. One stretch goal I have in mind is to verify the correctness of Chazelle's deterministic linear time triangulation algorithm.

Does this sound interesting? Let me know if anybody has thoughts.
